title: Housing protesters clash with police in Lisbon and Porto

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against soaring housing costs, high house prices, and a new government rental bill.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand the government scrap plans to make evictions easier and end rent caps on new leases.
tea.changed: Nov 2: Demonstrators continued gathering in Rossio and Dom Joao I squares despite earlier police clearings.

summary: Thousands of housing protesters marched through central Lisbon and Porto to protest against soaring housing costs and a government rental bill. Following peaceful demonstrations, participants set up camps in Lisbon's Rossio Square and Porto's Dom Joao I Square. Early Sunday morning, dozens of police officers used shields and batons to dismantle the camps and disperse the participants. Activist group Acampada Lisboa organised responses and condemned the police intervention. Demonstrators are demanding that the minority center-right government withdraw its legislative plans that would facilitate evictions and remove rent caps on new leases. Prime Minister Luis Montenegro has stated that the bill will not be withdrawn, though modifications remain possible.

End rent caps on new leases

updates.text: Thousands of housing protesters marched through central Lisbon and Porto against rental legislation and housing costs.
Police moved in to dismantle camps in Lisbon's Rossio Square and Porto's Dom Joao I Square, leading to clashes.
Manifestants continued to maintain a presence at Rossio and Praça D. João I squares.
